channel.title: Churn Is Dead
channel.description: Weekly CS frameworks for enterprise Customer Success leaders. Hard truths, tactical plays, and downloadable playbooks.

item.title: Digital CS Is Not Coverage Until Someone Owns the Silence
item.description: Replace send volume and login counts with a Silence Ledger that shows who was reached, who responded, what changed, and when a human must step in.

item.title: The Renewal Is Not Yours to Own. The Change Order Is.
item.description: CS imported professional services' 'do whatever it takes' ethos and left behind the one discipline that made it survivable: the change order.

item.title: The CSM Title Is Now a Liability. The Rebrand Everyone's Reaching For Won't Fix It.
item.description: Renaming your CSMs to Forward Deployed Engineers fixes your recruiting funnel and moves your credibility gap to the exact place the customer finds it later: the renewal.

item.title: The 125% NRR That No CSM Ever Touched
item.description: In consumption pricing, your best NRR quarters are the ones you deserve the least credit for. Here's the spreadsheet that separates the retention you caused from the retention you witnessed.

item.title: You Don't Own NRR. You Rent It From Pricing.
item.description: Most of your NRR is inherited from the pricing model, not earned by your team. Here's how to prove it, and how to earn a seat in the room that actually moves the number.

item.title: Onboarding Isn't the Start of Retention. It's the Only Renewal You'll Ever Fully Control.
item.description: By the time the health score turns yellow in month nine, you're not preventing churn. You're documenting a decision made three quarters ago, during the one phase you actually controlled.

item.title: The Renewal Clause Your Lawyers Wrote and Your CS Team Forgot
item.description: The fastest NRR in your portfolio this year isn't in your expansion pipeline. It's in your filing cabinet, in the escalator clause nobody enforced.

item.title: The Two-Vendor Trick: How CS Platforms Quietly Became Org Charts You Can't Edit
item.description: You bought a CS platform to operationalize your strategy. Instead it operationalized the vendor's. Here's how to find out which decisions you never actually made.

item.title: The Expansion Recession Is Here. Stop Calling It a Retention Problem.
item.description: When gross retention holds but net retention falls, the problem isn't churn. It's an expansion ceiling set by pricing and roadmap. Here's how to decompose your NRR before leadership blames you for it.

item.title: The Day Your CSM Got Promoted to Babysitter
item.description: AI isn't killing the CSM role. It's quietly demoting it into babysitting automated busywork while leadership calls it transformation. Here's the job that actually survives.

item.title: The Renewal Cliff Nobody Charted: Why CS Doesn't Own Half the Churn It's Blamed For
item.description: Your churn model isn't getting smarter. It's getting more confident about the half of the problem it can see, and staying blind to the half that kills renewals.

item.title: CS Teams Don't Have a Churn Problem. They Have a Courage Problem.
item.description: CS teams have become professional excuse-makers who optimize for customer comfort instead of customer outcomes.

item.title: 3 Things Your CFO Knows About CS That You Don't
item.description: CFOs measure CS impact through financial models that most CS leaders don't understand—and those hidden metrics determine your budget.

item.title: The 30-Minute Monthly Business Review
item.description: QBRs waste executive time by reporting on history instead of driving decisions. Here's the Monthly Business Review that actually moves the needle.

item.title: Stop Scheduling Success: The Continuous CS Operating Model
item.description: QBRs are elaborate customer success theater. The highest-retention SaaS companies deliver success through continuous, in-product experiences instead.

item.title: I Stopped Tracking Health Scores. Here's What I Found Instead.
item.description: Health scores predict the past, not the future. Here's how to focus on what actually drives churn.

item.title: The Case Against Customer Health Scores
item.description: Health scores are the astrology of customer success—providing false confidence while real churn drivers remain invisible.

item.title: Your AI Customer Success Strategy Is Actually Firing People
item.description: CS leaders are using AI transformation as cover for headcount reduction while selling it as productivity enhancement.

item.title: Your AI Strategy Is Just Expensive Layoffs
item.description: CS leaders are using AI transformation as cover for workforce reduction while pretending it's about efficiency.

item.title: Your CS Platform Is A $200K Spreadsheet
item.description: Most CS platforms create expensive busywork instead of customer outcomes. Here's how to audit what you actually need.
